## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pāṭihāriyakathā* ("Discussion of Demonstrations") is a treatise in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, situated within the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994]. Formally enumerated among the thirty treatises forming the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the text adopts an analytical, Abhidhamma-style exposition of themes inherited from the early discourses [Hazra 1994]. Specifically, it elaborates upon the classical threefold classification of marvels or demonstrations: the miracle of psychic potency (*iddhi* or *iddhipāṭihāriya*), the marvel of thought-reading or telepathic discernment (*ādesanā*), and the superior marvel of pedagogical instruction (*anusāsanī*) [Hazra 1994].

SuttaCentral notes that the subject matter directly corresponds to discourse formulations found in the *Saṅgāravasutta* (AN 3.60) and the *Kevaṭṭa Sutta* (DN 11) [SuttaCentral]. Quantitative text-reuse analysis from DharmaNexus confirms these connections, identifying extensive Pali-internal matches: the largest textual overlaps occur with the *Tikanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (55 matches, notably AN 3.60 across segments §2.5–4.7 with 0.94 similarity) and the *Kevaṭṭa Sutta* (DN 11, §1.1–2.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns significant passages of the text with the *Sampasādanīya Sutta* (DN 28), the *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48), the *Iddhipāda Saṁyutta* (SN 51), several sections of the Aṅguttara (AN 4, AN 5, AN 6, AN 7, AN 10) and Majjhima Nikāyas (MN 66, MN 67, MN 70, MN 139), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects cross-linguistic alignments with the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* and Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna and scholastic works, including the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā* [DharmaNexus].
